title: Stroke and antithrombotics in pregnancy and postpartum
keyNumbers: Antiplatelet needed: Aspirin <100 mg daily first choice (safe in lactation; no hold for neuraxial); clopidogrel for the shortest needed duration; ticagrelor/prasugrel minimal data
Neuraxial anesthesia timing: Aspirin: no hold; prophylactic LMWH ≥12 h; therapeutic LMWH ≥24 h; low-dose UFH 4–6 h
Enoxaparin — prophylactic: 40 mg daily (or 30 mg q12h) — fixed dosing preferred to weight-based for prophylaxis in pregnancy
Mechanical valve, warfarin >5 mg/day needed: Dose-adjusted LMWH ≥BID (anti-Xa 0.8–1.2 U/mL 4–6 h post-dose) in first trimester, then warfarin; IV UFH (aPTT 2× control) if LMWH unavailable
question: Which acute treatments and antithrombotics are used in pregnancy, postpartum and lactation?
population: Pregnant or postpartum patients with stroke or a stroke-prevention indication

rules.recommendation: Don't delay standard treatment. IVT when benefit outweighs risk (alteplase and TNK don't cross the placenta; TNK data limited); individualize with planned or recent cesarean or neuraxial anesthesia
EVT as in nonpregnant patients; transradial approach preferred; consider continuous fetal monitoring in third trimester
Aspirin <100 mg daily first choice (safe in lactation; no hold for neuraxial); clopidogrel for the shortest needed duration; ticagrelor/prasugrel minimal data
LMWH first choice (safe in lactation); UFH safe; warfarin teratogenic in first trimester (select mechanical-valve cases after) and safe in lactation; DOACs — insufficient data

rules.condition: Secondary prevention after prior ischemic stroke/TIA
rules.recommendation: Low-dose aspirin for most; therapeutic LMWH for antiphospholipid syndrome, mechanical valve or prior cardioembolic stroke

rules.condition: Cryptogenic stroke with PFO, planning pregnancy
rules.recommendation: PFO closure may be considered before a future pregnancy if RoPE ≥7
Full-dose LMWH throughout pregnancy, then LMWH or VKA ≥6 weeks postpartum (≥3 months total); LMWH prophylaxis in future pregnancies
Therapeutic anticoagulation with frequent monitoring; shared decision on strategy

rules.condition: Mechanical valve, warfarin ≤5 mg/day keeps INR therapeutic
rules.recommendation: Continuing warfarin through all trimesters is reasonable after counseling
Dose-adjusted LMWH ≥BID (anti-Xa 0.8–1.2 U/mL 4–6 h post-dose) in first trimester, then warfarin; IV UFH (aPTT 2× control) if LMWH unavailable
Warfarin → BID LMWH or IV UFH ≥1 week before; LMWH → UFH ≥36 h before; stop UFH ≥6 h before vaginal delivery; labor on warfarin → cesarean after reversal
Aspirin: no hold; prophylactic LMWH ≥12 h; therapeutic LMWH ≥24 h; low-dose UFH 4–6 h

options.doseText: 40 mg daily (or 30 mg q12h) — fixed dosing preferred to weight-based for prophylaxis in pregnancy
1 mg/kg q12h or 1.5 mg/kg daily; mechanical valve: dose-adjust to anti-Xa 0.8–1.2 U/mL
evidenceNote: Miller 2026 Table 2; Otto 2020 for anti-Xa target

contraindications: Warfarin in the first trimester outside mechanical-valve decisions
institutionVaries: Maternal stroke alert pathway (L&D vs ED) and MFM/anesthesia co-management
pearls: Miller 2026 is an AHA scientific statement endorsed by ACOG (January 2026); per its title page it "should be construed as ACOG clinical guidance"
sources: Miller EC, et al. Prevention and Treatment of Maternal Stroke in Pregnancy and Postpartum: A Scientific Statement From the AHA (endorsed by ACOG). Stroke 2026;57:e127-e145. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000514
